classification: Conceptual illustration; not a measurement, actual audio-device photograph, software UI, or experimental result.
prompt: Create a premium surreal editorial conceptual illustration for an educational audio-mixing carousel, 6:5 landscape image, with a bright seamless white background. Show a beautifully designed miniature white stage or low white architectural platform in a diagonal three-quarter perspective, using theatrical composition to express temporary musical attention and local space-making. Only three visual groups: in the left-middle of the stage, a compact cobalt-blue sculptural rising flare made of several refined translucent angular fins, suggesting a musical transition effect; at the front-right, one elegant unbranded silver vocal microphone on a slim stand, fully visible and distinctly important; toward the rear-left, a few quiet low matte light-gray accompaniment planes gently receding in depth. The blue transition sculpture briefly occupies one soft pool of light, while the microphone has its own soft clear pool of light. Both remain intact and legible: this is a momentary handover of attention, not the effect permanently overpowering the vocal and not everything else being switched off. The gray backing shapes subtly step back without disappearing. Keep the stage airy, minimal and physically dimensional. No human performers, no audience, no concert truss, no stage curtains, no instrument collection, no headphones, no mixing console, no drum. The strong silhouette should be two distinct focal subjects and a quiet background, with generous occupancy of the frame and clean white outer margins. Palette: dominant white #ffffff and subtle neutral #f5f5f7, precise restrained cobalt blue #0066cc, brushed-silver microphone, fine natural shadows. High-key premium studio rendering, soft cinematic lighting without a dark backdrop; avoid heavy gradients, neon, purple, orange and dramatic black shadows. No typography, no words, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no labels, no timeline, no arrows, no software UI, no graph or measured waveform. Clearly a conceptual illustration of musical priority, not a real venue, plugin screenshot or measured audio result.
